stops.name: Nelson Piquet
stops.note: derived: 'As the front half of the field started lap 21 Piquet peeled off into the pit lane' (he ran in the leading train), so in-lap 20; rejoined 15th

stops.name: Alain Prost
stops.note: derived: 'at the start of lap 28 Prost swooped into the Ferrari pits', so in-lap 27; rejoined 8th. His stop lap was 1:26.712 against 1:10 laps

stops.name: Gerhard Berger
stops.note: derived: Motor Sport has Berger stopping after Prost, 'relinquishing the lead to Senna for a brief two laps'; Wikipedia's chart has Berger leading laps 1-27 and Senna 28-29. Stop lap 1:35.188. A second stop later (Wikipedia), no lap

stops.name: Ayrton Senna
stops.note: derived: led two laps (chart: 28-29) 'and then the Brazilian was in, handing the lead to Mansell' (chart: Mansell 30-31). A rear wheel baulked: stop lap 1:37.672

stops.name: Nigel Mansell
stops.note: derived: 'Mansell gave the lead to Patrese when he went into the pits for tyres' (chart: Patrese leads lap 32). A second stop later ('made a second stop for tyres', Motor Sport), no lap

stops.name: Riccardo Patrese
stops.note: derived: 'after one lap in the lead Patrese came in for tyres and it was Capelli's turn to lead'; Capelli 'took the lead at the end of lap 33' (Autosport archive)

runningOrder.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_French_Grand_Prix: 'Berger took the lead at the start followed by pole sitter Mansell, Senna, Nannini, Patrese, Prost, Boutsen, Piquet and Jean Alesi'
runningOrder.note: read as the order at the end of lap 1

runningOrder.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_French_Grand_Prix: 'Capelli took the lead being followed by teammate Gugelmin. Prost overtook Gugelmin on lap 54'

notes: Motor Sport Aug 1990 ('A Touch of the Sun', DSJ); Wikipedia's lap-leader chart; GrandPrix.com GPE rr491; Autosport archive feature. Capelli (#16) and Gugelmin (#15) ran non-stop: 'they did not come in for tyres ... still they stayed out on the same tyres' (Motor Sport); Leyton House was 'the only team to attempt to race without stopping for fresh tyres' (Wikipedia). Gugelmin's engine lost oil pressure a few laps after Prost passed him on lap 54 (Jolpica: 58 laps); Wikipedia's 'Gugelmin stopped late in the race' reads as that retirement, not a tyre stop. Prost passed Capelli for the lead on lap 78 (Motor Sport; Wikipedia's chart: Prost leads 78-80; Wikipedia's text says 'lap 77 of 80'); Capelli's Judd was hesitating out of slow corners (Motor Sport), an oil light and dropping fuel pressure (Capelli, Autosport archive). Missing: Alesi's (#4) tyre stop (his final drive failed leaving the pits; Jolpica 23 laps, no lap in any source), Nannini's (#19) stop, Berger's and Mansell's second stops, every midfield stop. Stop laps for Berger, Senna, Mansell and Patrese are worked out from the leader chart and Motor Sport's order, not quoted.
